name: Live-to-repo harness drift reconcile - with a both-states control on the tool itself
description: Blueprint 92 of 96 (design BP-MNT-01). Reconcile the live harness trees against the repo WITHOUT the reconciliation tool destroying uncommitted repo work. Mechanism: the workflow's FIRST stage is a both-states control on the sync tool in a scratch copy - prove that a bare `-Report json` run destroys an uncommitted edit and that `-Drift` does not - and the run is gated on that proof. The deterministic classification half is DELEGATED to the dual-tree-plumbing-mirror subworkflow rather than reimplemented, so there is exactly one blob-classification implementation in the platform. What remains here is what only this workflow does: distrust a tool whose flag semantics are a live hazard, and route two-sided files to a human two-directional merge.

live_roots.description: ABSOLUTE live harness roots (e.g. the skills, hooks and rules trees). Live-only work is architecturally orphaned until it lands in the repo.

repo_root.description: ABSOLUTE repo root - the source of truth. The live tree is a deploy target, never the authority.

mode.description: drift = measure only. apply = write. A bare report flag is NOT a mode: on the measured tool it selects the OUTPUT FORMAT and still writes.

scratch_copy_root.description: ABSOLUTE path to a throwaway copy where the both-states control on the tool is run. The control must never run against the real repo.

allow_apply_with_dirty_repo.description: Must stay false. The tool's pre-write guard reads STAGED paths only, so unstaged and untracked repo work is unprotected during an apply.

control-runner.description: Runs the both-states control on the sync tool in a scratch copy and reports whether the footgun reproduces on THIS box today

merge-author.description: Performs the two-directional hand merge for files where both the live tree and the repo hold unique content

owner.description: The human owner - decides which branch carries the reconciliation PR and authorises any apply

routes.reason: a two-directional merge that drops one side's unique lines is unrecoverable data loss, so it gets maximum effort

repo-clean-before-apply.expression: mode == drift OR repo_uncommitted_paths == 0 OR allow_apply_with_dirty_repo == true

stages.title: Both-states control: prove the footgun reproduces, in a scratch copy

work_unit.title: Reproduce and refute the sync-tool write footgun in a throwaway copy before trusting any run
work_unit.question_or_target: In scratch_copy_root: make a deliberate UNCOMMITTED repo edit, run the sync tool with a bare report flag, and record whether the edit survived. Then restore the edit and run the tool in drift mode and record whether it survived. The control must FIRE in the first state and be SILENT in the second - a probe silent in both states measures nothing.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the whole point of this stage is detector discipline, which is where this program has repeatedly lost

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the byte content of the deliberate edit before and after EACH of the two runs, plus both literal command lines; a claim that the footgun exists without the destroyed-then-preserved pair is a citation, not a measurement
tests_required: the control must FIRE (edit destroyed) on the bare-report run
the control must be SILENT (edit preserved) on the drift run
a control that reports the same outcome in both states must FAIL the stage - it proves the probe, not the tool
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader who confirms from the recorded bytes that the two runs differed in outcome, without re-running the tool
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9201 emitted only when both states were exercised and produced DIFFERENT outcomes; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9201 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry against the real repo under any circumstance; a scratch-copy failure is re-run once after re-creating the scratch copy, then escalated

stages.title: No run at all until the control has both states
Commit or stage every authoritative repo edit BEFORE any writing run

work_unit.title: Enumerate uncommitted repo work and require it to be committed or staged
work_unit.question_or_target: Run `git status --porcelain -uall` in repo_root and enumerate every modified, staged, and untracked path. Report the count of paths that are UNSTAGED or UNTRACKED - those are the ones the tool's pre-write guard does not protect.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: cheap, but the consequence of getting it wrong is unrecoverable

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the porcelain output with -uall and the three counts (staged, unstaged, untracked) derived from it; without -uall an untracked DIRECTORY collapses to one line and its members are invisible
tests_required: an untracked directory containing three files must contribute three paths, not one - the -uall control
a repo with unstaged work and mode=apply must fail the precondition gate
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the gate is the reviewer; the counts are re-derivable from the recorded porcelain output
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9202 emitted only when the -uall enumeration is recorded with all three counts; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9202 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - a git status that fails twice is an environment fault, and this workflow must never proceed on a guess about repo cleanliness

stages.title: The tool's guard reads STAGED paths only
Delegate the deterministic classification to the plumbing mirror
Two-directional merge - only for files where BOTH sides hold unique content

work_unit.title: Merge one two-sided file keeping every unique line from BOTH sides
work_unit.question_or_target: For one TWO-SIDED file, produce a merged version that retains the live tree's unique content AND the repo's unique content. Before writing, enumerate the lines unique to each side and assert both sets survive in the output.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a one-directional read cannot see two-directional divergence; the measured error direction on exactly this task was 31 of 31 pointing at data loss

work_unit.evidence_requirement: for each merged file the set of lines unique to the live side, the set unique to the repo side, and an assertion that BOTH sets appear in the merged output; a diff summary is not sufficient
tests_required: a merge that drops any line unique to either side must FAIL the unique-line assertion
both-states control: a deliberately one-directional merge (repo-only) must be caught by the same assertion, proving the assertion is not vacuous
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reviewer who re-derives the two unique-line sets from the raw blobs rather than from the merge author's summary
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9203 emitted only when the unique-line assertion holds for both sides; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9203 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: after two failed merges of the same file, hand it to the owner with both sides' unique-line sets rather than attempting a third

stages.title: The drift report, with the verdict's provenance attached

work_unit.title: Emit the drift report stating which run produced the verdict and whether that run wrote
work_unit.question_or_target: Emit the drift report with new / changed / identical / eol-only sets, the unresolved set, and - as a first-class field - which run produced the verdict and whether that run was non-writing. A CLEAN verdict from a writing run is not evidence of no drift.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: assembling a verdict with its provenance is judgement about what the evidence supports

work_unit.evidence_requirement: every set enumerated with counts, plus the run provenance (command line, mode, writing yes/no) that produced the verdict; a verdict whose producing run is unrecorded declares zero signals, not one
tests_required: an EOL-only pair must not appear in the changed set
a report whose producing run wrote must be rejected by the clean-verdict gate even if the sets look empty
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reviewer who checks the run provenance field before reading any set
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9204 emitted only when every set is enumerated AND the producing run's provenance is recorded; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9204 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - the report is assembled from artifacts on disk; a failure means one is missing or malformed

stages.title: A CLEAN verdict from a writing run is not evidence
Which branch carries the reconciliation PR
stages.prompt: The drift report is attached, two-sided files are merged with both sides' unique lines preserved, and the unresolved set is named. Which branch carries the reconciliation PR, and is an apply authorised?

estimate.measurement_source: 09-WORKFLOW-BLUEPRINT-LIBRARY.md#BP-MNT-01 - the measured tool footgun (a bare report-format flag WRITES, omits new/changed from the unresolved set, and still reports CLEAN with exit 0) and the ~470 lines of unversioned security-bearing live harness work it recovers

impact.blast_radius: in drift mode: read-only plus writes under command-center/drift/**. In apply mode it can overwrite repo files with live bytes - which is exactly why the both-states control and the commit-first gate precede it. A destroyed uncommitted edit is NOT recoverable.

x_extensions.mechanism: distrust-the-tool-first. The workflow's own first stage is a both-states control on the tool it is about to use, and the run is gated on that control having produced DIFFERENT outcomes in the broken and fixed states. The deterministic blob classification is delegated, not duplicated.

not_a_duplicate_because.vs_dual-tree-plumbing-mirror: that primitive has no tool to distrust and no merge path - it refuses two-sided paths. This workflow CALLS it (declared in subworkflows, invoked by the classify-drift stage) and adds the two things only it does: a both-states control on a hazardous tool, and a two-directional hand merge whose postcondition is that BOTH sides' unique lines survive.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_anchor-checked-per-file-deploy: that is the safe TRANSPORT that lands a change once a drift verdict exists; this produces the verdict. The dependency runs one way: deploy consumes drift-report.json.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_pre-pr-surface-check: that compares two COMMITS in one repo; this compares two TREES on disk, one of which is not under version control at all.

contraindications: NOT for application repos with a normal workflow
NOT while a peer session holds the checkout - a concurrent write makes every hash comparison a race

benchmark_cases.given: a scratch copy with an uncommitted repo edit and a bare report-format run
benchmark_cases.expect: the edit is DESTROYED - the control fires. Then with -Drift the same edit survives. Different outcomes in the two states is the pass condition.

benchmark_cases.given: a live/repo pair differing only in line endings
benchmark_cases.expect: classified EOL-ONLY and absent from the changed set

benchmark_cases.given: a deliberately repo-only merge of a two-sided file
benchmark_cases.expect: the unique-line assertion FAILS, proving it is not vacuous

control_result.broken_state_run: bare -Report json -> the uncommitted edit to hooks/_shared/completion.py was overwritten with live bytes; control FIRED
control_result.fixed_state_run: -Drift -Report json -> the same edit survived byte-for-byte; control SILENT
control_result.verdict: PASS - different outcomes in the two states

worked_examples.terminal_state: SUCCESS:BPW-9204 - drift report emitted from a NON-writing run, provenance recorded, 2 files merged with both sides' unique lines asserted present
worked_examples.note: The 7 EOL-only files would have appeared as drift under a naive comparison. The 2 two-sided files are the ones a one-directional check would have silently overwritten - the measured error direction on this exact task was 31 of 31 pointing at data loss.

x_extensions.owner_decision: YES - where the ~470 lines of unversioned, security-bearing live harness work land: which branch carries the PR. Represented in-workflow as the owner-branch-decision human checkpoint, so the workflow cannot silently pick for the owner.
unverified: That the footgun still reproduces on this box TODAY is UNVERIFIED by this artifact - that is precisely why stage control-the-tool exists and why the whole run is gated on it. The design card's confidence is almost-certain (90-99%) that it exists as documented; this workflow refuses to inherit that confidence and re-measures it every run. Settling experiment = stage control-the-tool itself.
The ~470-line figure for unversioned live harness work is quoted from the design card and is NOT re-measured here. Settling experiment = the classify-drift stage's new_in_live line count.
